domain: Moral Philosophy / Historical Ethics / Developmental Biology
topic_summary: Analysis of Spartan infant exposure practice as a test case for contested moral-standing boundaries across time. The historical Spartan reading (hillside exposure as legitimate population regulation) versus modern readings (categorical infanticide prohibition) instantiate structurally different constraints from a shared personhood-boundary kernel. Tests whether the Spartan reading 'dropped' (became untenable within the kernel) or 'left the space' (kernel itself transformed).

key_entities: Spartan gerousia (council of elders with infant-examination authority)
Exposed infants (victims under modern reading, non-persons under Spartan reading)
Taygetus hillside (physical exposure site, ritual boundary marker)
key_tensions: State population-management authority vs infant life-protection (Spartan gerousia vs modern categorical prohibition)
Community-viability threshold vs individual-life sanctity (eugenic reading vs rights-based reading)
key_mechanisms: Gerousia examination ritual (determiner of fitness/personhood eligibility)
Hillside exposure (execution method framing infant as not-yet-person)
Modern prosecutorial apparatus (enforcement of categorical infanticide prohibition)
key_absences: Spartan maternal voice in examination process (exposure was state decision, not parental)
Developmental-continuity argument (gradual personhood acquisition vs threshold)
Cross-cultural exposure practices (Sparta not unique; Viking, Roman, Chinese parallels unaddressed)

axiom_contradictions.basis: No coherent framework can hold both 'live birth confers inviolable personhood' and 'pre-confirmation infants are legitimately excludable'—accepting either axiom requires rejecting the other's personhood threshold
Eugenic reading requires binary threshold (confirmed/unconfirmed); developmental reading denies any binary threshold exists—frameworks are structurally incompatible
Categorical birth-threshold requires discrete moral boundary; developmental reading requires continuous acquisition of moral weight—no framework holds both simultaneously without contradiction

omegas.description: Did the Spartan reading 'drop' (became untenable within the kernel due to new evidence/arguments) or 'leave the space' (the kernel itself transformed such that the reading no longer addresses the same question)? Developmental biology did not exist in Sparta—does its emergence change the kernel or merely add a new reading?

Spartan exposure was state-controlled (gerousia decision), not parental. Modern frameworks assume parental authority over infant care decisions. The absence of maternal voice in Spartan practice may indicate a separate axis (parental vs state authority over children) that the personhood-boundary kernel does not capture.

Exposure practices in Viking, Roman, Chinese cultures suggest the Spartan reading was not unique. If multiple independent cultures converged on similar readings, does this indicate a structural constraint (resource scarcity + pre-industrial infant mortality) that modern readings ignore? Or does convergence merely reflect shared ignorance?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + deferred cross-cultural analysis

omegas.description: Spartan exposure was ritualized (Taygetus hillside, gerousia examination). Modern infanticide is prosecuted regardless of method. Does ritualization signal that Spartans recognized moral weight (hence needed ritual justification) or that they denied moral weight (ritual as bureaucratic sorting, not moral deliberation)?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)—ritual may obscure extraction by military state

omegas.description: We possess developmental neuroscience; Spartans did not. Does this epistemic asymmetry make the Spartan reading 'unreachable' in the sense of 'no longer justifiable given available evidence' or 'no longer addressable because the question changed'? If the former, the reading dropped; if the latter, it left.
omegas.source: Core kernel/reading decomposition question; connects to F34 concern
